newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Labour says plans speedy action on tube.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Labour says plans speedy action on tube.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour party said on Wednesday that, if elected, it would be in a position to act quickly to address the funding crisis within the London Underground rail system, but stressed it would stick to the existing budget.

Labour transport spokesman Andrew Smith told Reuters in an interview: "We're in consultation with financial experts and London Transport over options and we are confident we will be able to move quickly once elected."
He added Labour would "adhere to the existing budget constraints", appearing to rule out any emergency cash injection into the network.
Smith said that he had already started talks with relevant groups, with an election looming and due by May 22 at the latest.
He said talks with London Transport, the nationalised body repsonsible for the metro, had been "positive and helpful" to date.
Labour has ruled out the privatisation of the metro -- the policy of the ruling Conservative Party, which has pledged to raise up to two billion stg from the sale if it wins the election.

Labour has not expanded greatly on how public-private partnerships could work in practice. But a Labour spokeswoman added that it wished to see strategic control remain in public hands on issues like service standards, safety and travel cards.
"There is scope for private sector expertise in capital investments to get a better system," she said.

One option under consideration includes franchising of metro lines but retaining overall public control. Labour said it would issue a more detailed policy statement on the tube in the run-up to the election.
